dna.fixture_why: The artifact stands as the whole ladder by default, which is what it is for. The SWEEP must see one rung at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so an all-rungs view in the same spec frames every single rung against a row several times its width and photographs it as a speck. That is not a hypothetical - it crashed the critic on a subject box too small to sample.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 50.4% of frame width and 21.1% of its height, with a subject share of 4.24%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.27. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: ultra against fine, in the sample reading
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Bilinear error on a smooth surface falls as h^2. fine is h = 1/16, ultra is h = 1/32, so ultra's error is a quarter of fine's and the pair differs by the 3/4 of an error that is already small. 1.2%.
predicted_degeneracy.registered: 2026-08-15, BEFORE the first capture. RESTORED the same day after tools/apply_dna_block.py's lazy regex swallowed this key while re-deriving an empty axes object; text verbatim from the pre-registration.

sampling_bench.description: One analytic surface sampled at the four densities the family names - coarse, mid, fine, ultra - with the gap between sample and surface drawn as struts standing where the error occurs. The only ladder in the wave with a limit object underneath it.
